title: Flashback Table offered as the rollback for a dropped column
expected_feedback: Critical: the stated rollback does not work, which is more dangerous than having no rollback at all — it will be approved on the strength of a recovery step that fails when invoked. Oracle cannot flash a table back across a DDL that changed its structure, and 'modifying or dropping a column' is explicitly on the blocking list alongside MOVE, TRUNCATE, adding a constraint and most partition maintenance. The FLASHBACK TABLE statement here will error, not restore. Match the tool to the damage: Flashback Table TO TIMESTAMP is for bad DML with no structural change since; Flashback Table TO BEFORE DROP is for an un-purged DROP TABLE and is unaffected by this rule; structural DDL needs a pre-DDL artefact — a keyed CTAS snapshot of the dropped column, a guaranteed restore point, or verified RMAN backup for PITR. Take it before the DROP and record which one in the rollback plan; classify the phase restore/PITR.
violated_rule: Recovery paths must be ones Oracle actually supports
